# Native stroke holdouts

Original DrawingML generated by `tools/outline_stroke_holdouts_fixture.py`,
using original curve-control OPC boilerplate and no renderer serialization.
Each 384×256 CSS-pixel page contains eight paths: preset ellipse, equivalent
cubic ellipse, open cubic, and triangle, repeated on two rows.

- `rotation-alpha`: 15° opaque strokes; 45° strokes at 50% opacity.
- `alpha-only`: 50% opacity, first unrotated and then at 15°. This separates
  opacity from rotation rather than inferring one from the combined case.
- `dash-compound`: four dashed strokes and four 2pt double-line strokes.
  **The open compound cubic (ID 7) is unsupported and omitted in the preview.**
  Its seven siblings remain visible; the document is read-only. The three
  supported closed compound shapes are IDs 5, 6 and 8.

All single pens are 4327 EMU, opaque color C0C0C0 before any alpha transform.
Offsets use the same .53-pixel phase on both axes. Authored values remain intact.

Exact private copies were opened with the reference-application helper and displayed by the reference application
without repair. Six native captures use 100%/200% zoom and a
1280×752 viewport. The recorder verifies source package entries, screenshot
format/size and neutral colors in 48 fixed regions. Regions exclude the page's
left-side caret. Origins are observed page edges (439,326 at 100%; 247,212 at
200%), never fitted to artwork. The native originals are JPEG; PNG crops retain
compression artifacts. Mean pixel differences rank experiments only and do not
prove an opacity law or exact native antialiasing.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses: §20.1.2.2.24 (`ln`), §20.1.10.35 (physical
line width), §20.1.2.3.1 (alpha), §20.1.8.48 (preset dash) and §20.1.10.15
(compound line types). The supplied specification was read locally. These
physical/color declarations do not prescribe device-grid snapping.

Run the generator, obtain native captures through the documented reference-application UI,
then run `tools/record_outline_stroke_holdouts.py <private-work-directory>`.
`node tools/diagnose-outline-stroke-candidate.mjs <private-output-directory>`
runs isolated baseline/adaptive/dash experiments on Vite port 5173. Pass that
output directory as the recorder's second argument to regenerate comparison
evidence. No production source is modified by the experiment.

The adaptive path hints only axis-aligned single outlines and retains at least
2× raster density. The dash variant also preserves physical dash lengths while
hinting pen width. It improves the transparent and dashed samples but changes
raster phase for other content; the closed compound controls still regress.
The original planner looks stronger under the experiment, but that is not a
shipping gate. Open compound-path support, unchanged raster behavior for other
content, and effects/mixed-content controls remain necessary. No production
outline fix or corpus promotion is claimed.
